confidence_notes: I ran two web searches: one for the RBA rate and one for Interlaken prices. The price search returned individual venue menus, not an aggregated index. Cappuccino was about 5.60–8 CHF and draft beer 6–7 CHF per 300ml, from those menus. The inexpensive-meal and mid-range-meal figures are estimates; the search found no reliable Interlaken average, only a Lauterbrunnen review citing roughly 20–30 CHF for mains. Cocktail and wine are set from the local beer price using typical ratios, not from direct Interlaken price data. All four accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge for July peak season, not live listings, and are the least certain. I assumed about 1.25 USD per CHF for conversion.
comparable_city_reasoning: Priced as a high-cost Swiss Alpine tourist town, comparable to Lucerne and Grindelwald. Interlaken is slightly below Zurich for restaurant prices, but July peak-season demand pushes accommodation up.
